text:
morgan: quick sync? hit a mismatch wiring auth headers between hosted control-plane and private adapters, causing request drops in private canaries.
raj: paste a sample? is this the x-tenant vs x-caller-id thing?
tess: saw this earlier — private deployments intentionally strip some incoming headers for local security, but we don't have a clear translation layer.
morgan: example: hosted control-plane sends `authorization: Bearer <token>` + `x-tenant: org-123`. private adapter expects mTLS + `x-caller-id`. when control-plane connects we end up with neither and request rejected.
raj: options: 1) normalize in control-plane (add a translation step based on deployment mode), 2) adapters accept both header shapes, or 3) add a gateway/rewrite proxy.
tess: lean to #1 (normalize at control-plane) because it's central and keeps adapters thin. but careful: we must not accidentally translate customer-managed KMS headers into hosted KMS tokens. sensitive header policy needed.
morgan: agreed. we should record any header rewriting with an audit marker so SRE/security can trace changes — e.g. add `x-rw-proxied: header_translation=v1` when a rewrite happens.
raj: also think about function/tool-call semantics: private envs often block outbound webhooks. we need an explicit capability flag so customers don't get surprise failures. propose `no_external_calls` in the capability manifest.
tess: +1. general approach: keep the API surface the same for devs, but require a capability negotiation during control-plane <-> adapter handshake. capabilities is a small JSON list like: ```capabilities: ["kms_customer","header_translation","no_external_calls"]``` Defaults: if absent, assume `minimal` (no translations, no external calls).
morgan: i'll sketch a capability manifest and minimal translation shim this week and open a PR. will include examples for mapping headers and audit tagging.
raj: :thumbsup: include unit tests asserting header preservation and tests for the audit tag.
tess: and add a `hosting.mode` telemetry field so logs/metrics can be grouped by hosted/dedicated/private for regression analysis.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: noted, created RFC draft link: https://go/rfcs/rw-hosting-handshake-translation (WIP).
morgan: thanks — i'll connect the branch to the RFC and ping when ready for review.
